notes: the ADR-0013 while-lowering shape (c is indices 3-5, lenC 3; A is indices 7-11, lenA 5): pop_jump_if_falsy at index 6 takes lenA + 2 = 7 and lands on index 13; jump_backward at index 12 takes lenC + lenA + 1 = 9 and lands on index 3, the condition's first instruction. No compiler emits jump_backward yet (ISA v6, tier 9), so this is hand-authored rather than source-based.

the same shape as counted-loop-runs-to-completion, with i initialized to 5 instead of 0: the condition (i < 3) is falsy on the very first check, so pop_jump_if_falsy takes the loop's exit branch immediately and the back edge is never taken.

a minimal loop whose body assigns i = 1 outright (not i + 1), so the condition (i < 1) is true exactly once: the back edge at index 10 is taken exactly once before the condition flips false on the second check, pinning jump_backward's own target arithmetic (index - offset) independently of the counted-loop shape above.

an unconditionally infinite loop - the condition is always true, so pop_jump_if_falsy always falls through and jump_backward always fires - exhausts any finite loop budget. This pins the error type and reason (ADR-0013), not the count at which any particular implementation's default budget fires; the shipping default is Predicator.Evaluator.default_loop_budget/0 (10,000 back edges), which this case runs at since the corpus's evaluate_case/2 passes no evaluation options.
jump_backward's offset must be a positive integer (docs/isa.md section 2's standing malformed-operand rule); 0 fails the guard and falls through to the catch-all clause.

the back edge's target (index - offset) would be before index 0 - jump_backward is at index 1 with offset 5, targeting -4 - so the guard fails and this falls through to the catch-all unknown_instruction clause, same as a positive out-of-range offset would.
